subject: accountancy

concepts.title: Meaning and Definition of Accounting
concepts.definition: A structured methodology for tracking, quantifying, documenting, and sharing financial data of a business entity to assist stakeholders in making choices.
concepts.key_idea: Accounting acts as an information system that translates business activities into financial reports.
question_patterns: define the term accounting
what is the meaning of accounting
explain the concept of accounting as an information system
how is accounting defined by the AICPA
describe the fundamental meaning of accounting

solution_steps.action: Identify the core components of the accounting definition
solution_steps.explain: Accounting involves identifying, measuring, recording, and communicating financial information.

concepts.title: Economic Events
concepts.definition: Significant financial occurrences within or outside an enterprise that involve measurable transactions expressed in monetary units.
concepts.key_idea: Transactions must be measurable in monetary terms to be considered economic events.
question_patterns: what is an economic event in accounting
distinguish between internal and external economic events
give examples of external economic events
how do you define an economic event
explain internal economic events with examples

solution_steps.action: Classify the event as internal or external
solution_steps.explain: External events involve transactions with outsiders, while internal events occur entirely within the enterprise.

concepts.title: The Accounting Process
concepts.definition: The series of actions involving the recognition, monetary valuation, chronological bookkeeping, and reporting of business transactions to interested parties.
concepts.key_idea: The process begins with identification of transactions and ends with communication of financial statements.
question_patterns: what are the steps in the accounting process
explain identification and measurement in accounting
how are economic events recorded and communicated
describe the chronological recording of transactions
what does communication of accounting information involve

solution_steps.action: Trace the sequence from identification to communication
solution_steps.explain: Transactions are first identified, then measured in money, recorded in books, and finally communicated via reports.

concepts.title: Users of Accounting Information
concepts.definition: Various stakeholders, split into inside managers and outside entities like lenders or regulators, who utilize financial statements for their specific analytical needs.
concepts.key_idea: Different stakeholders utilize accounting data to assess performance, solvency, and compliance.
question_patterns: who are the users of accounting information
distinguish between internal and external users of accounting
why do creditors need accounting information
identify the external users of financial statements
list the internal users of accounting reports

solution_steps.action: Determine if the user is internal or external
solution_steps.explain: Internal users are inside the management team, whereas external users are outside parties like investors and tax authorities.

concepts.title: Sub-disciplines of Accounting
concepts.definition: Distinct fields of study within accountancy designed for different purposes, including historical reporting to outsiders, tracking production expenses, and aiding internal managerial strategy.
concepts.key_idea: Different branches serve distinct informational needs of internal and external stakeholders.
question_patterns: what are the branches of accounting
explain the difference between financial and cost accounting
describe the role of management accounting
how does cost accounting assist management
list the sub-disciplines of accounting

solution_steps.action: Identify the branch based on the primary objective
solution_steps.explain: Financial accounting records past transactions, cost accounting analyzes manufacturing expenses, and management accounting aids future planning.

concepts.title: Qualitative Characteristics of Accounting Information
concepts.definition: Core features of financial reports - such as being dependable, timely, clear, and consistent - that ensure the presented data is highly valuable for analysis.
concepts.key_idea: Information must be timely, verifiable, clear, and consistent across periods and entities.
question_patterns: what are the qualitative characteristics of accounting information
explain reliability and relevance in accounting
how is comparability achieved in financial reports
why is understandability important in accounting
describe the attributes that make accounting information useful

solution_steps.action: Assess the qualitative attributes of the information
solution_steps.explain: The four main attributes are reliability, relevance, understandability, and comparability.

concepts.title: Objectives of Accounting
concepts.definition: The fundamental aims of bookkeeping, which center on keeping orderly transaction logs, determining net income, showing assets and liabilities, and distributing reports.
concepts.key_idea: Accounting aims to provide a true and fair view of financial performance and position.
question_patterns: what are the main objectives of accounting
how does accounting help in depicting financial position
explain the objective of maintaining systematic records
why is calculation of profit and loss an objective of accounting
describe the primary goals of accounting

solution_steps.action: Identify the primary goal of the accounting activity
solution_steps.explain: The main goals are record maintenance, profit calculation, financial position depiction, and information communication.

concepts.title: Basic Accounting Terms: Assets and Liabilities
concepts.definition: Assets represent valuable properties or rights controlled by a firm that yield future utility, whereas liabilities denote outstanding financial debts owed to external parties.
concepts.key_idea: Assets represent what the business owns, and liabilities represent what it owes to outsiders.
question_patterns: define assets and liabilities
what is the difference between current and non-current assets
explain current liabilities with examples
how are assets classified in a balance sheet
what do liabilities represent in accounting

solution_steps.action: Classify items into assets or liabilities
solution_steps.explain: Owned resources are assets, while obligations to pay in the future are liabilities.

concepts.title: Calculation of Accounting Profit
concepts.definition: The positive net earnings realized when a business's total periodic revenues exceed its corresponding operating costs.
concepts.key_idea: Profit is the positive difference between total revenue and total expenses.
question_patterns: calculate the profit when revenue is {revenue} and expenses are {expenses}
what is the profit if the total revenue is {revenue} and total expenses are {expenses}
find the profit earned by a business with revenue of {revenue} and expenses of {expenses}
determine the profit given revenue {revenue} and expenses {expenses}
how much profit is made when revenue is {revenue} and expenses are {expenses}

solution_steps.action: Calculate profit by subtracting expenses from revenue
solution_steps.explain: Profit is the excess of revenue over expenses.

concepts.title: Calculation of Accounting Loss
concepts.definition: The negative financial outcome that occurs when a firm's total operating expenditures surpass its total earned revenues over a given timeframe.
concepts.key_idea: Loss is the excess of expenses over revenues.
question_patterns: calculate the loss when expenses are {expenses} and revenue is {revenue}
what is the loss if total expenses are {expenses} and total revenue is {revenue}
find the loss incurred by a business with expenses of {expenses} and revenue of {revenue}
determine the loss given expenses {expenses} and revenue {revenue}
how much loss is suffered when expenses are {expenses} and revenue is {revenue}

solution_steps.action: Calculate loss by subtracting revenue from expenses
solution_steps.explain: Loss is the excess of expenses over revenue.

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values into the formula

worked_examples.question_pattern: calculate the loss when expenses are {expenses} and revenue is {revenue}

concepts.title: Calculation of Gain on Sale of Asset
concepts.definition: An irregular financial benefit resulting from non-operating transactions, such as disposing of a long-term resource for more than its carrying value.
concepts.key_idea: Gain is the excess of the selling price of an asset over its cost or book value.
question_patterns: calculate the gain when an asset costing {cost_price} is sold for {selling_price}
what is the gain if a machine of cost {cost_price} is sold for {selling_price}
find the gain on sale of an asset with cost price {cost_price} and selling price {selling_price}
determine the gain when selling price is {selling_price} and cost is {cost_price}
how much gain is earned if an asset worth {cost_price} is sold for {selling_price}

solution_steps.action: Calculate gain by subtracting cost price from selling price
solution_steps.explain: Gain is the excess of selling price over cost price.

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values into the formula

worked_examples.question_pattern: calculate the gain when an asset costing {selling_price} is sold for {cost_price}

concepts.title: Total Expenses and Losses
concepts.definition: The combined total of standard business operating costs and sudden non-reciprocal damages or asset destructions within a period.
concepts.key_idea: Combining operational expenses and incidental losses to find total financial outflows.
question_patterns: calculate the total of expenses and losses when expenses are {expenses} and losses are {losses}
what is the total amount of expenses and losses if expenses are {expenses} and losses are {losses}
find the sum of expenses of {expenses} and losses of {losses}
determine the total financial outflow given expenses {expenses} and losses {losses}
how much is the total of expenses {expenses} and losses {losses}

solution_steps.action: Calculate total outflow by adding expenses and losses
solution_steps.explain: Total outflow is the sum of expenses and losses.

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values into the formula

worked_examples.question_pattern: calculate the total of expenses and losses when expenses are {expenses} and losses are {losses}

concepts.title: Basic Accounting Terms: Capital and Drawings
concepts.definition: Capital is the financial investment made by a proprietor into a business, while drawings represent the extraction of cash or goods by the owner for personal use.
concepts.key_idea: Capital increases owner's equity, whereas drawings reduce it.
question_patterns: define capital and drawings in accounting
what is the difference between capital and drawings
how do drawings affect the owner's capital
explain the term capital with examples
what does drawings mean in business

solution_steps.explain: Capital is the owner's investment in the business, whereas drawings are the owner's personal withdrawals from the business.

concepts.title: Basic Accounting Terms: Debtors and Creditors
concepts.definition: Debtors are customers or entities who owe money to the business for credit sales, while creditors are suppliers to whom the business owes money for credit purchases.
concepts.key_idea: Debtors are current assets, whereas creditors are current liabilities.
question_patterns: distinguish between debtors and creditors
who is a debtor in business
explain the term creditors with examples
how are debtors and creditors shown in the balance sheet
what is the meaning of sundry debtors

solution_steps.explain: Debtors represent amounts receivable from customers, whereas creditors represent amounts payable to suppliers.
